item.title: Dispersive estimates for limit-periodic Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.31497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove dispersive estimates for limit-periodic operators that are super-exponentially well-approximated by periodic operators. The key ingredient is a sharp enhanced convexity statement for the density of states of periodic Jacobi matrices. This statement implies log-convexity of the density of states and hence is a strengthening of existing results on the convexity of equilibrium measures. We expect that it will be of interest and use outside of this work. We also construct almost-periodic discrete Schr\"odinger operators with purely singular continuous spectrum whose unitary groups enjoy recurrent dispersive motion: on one subsequence of time scales, the unitary group has a dispersive estimate at a rate as close to the free rate as one desires, while on another set of time scales, the unitary group is as far from dispersive as possible. In fact, this behavior is generic within the class of limit-periodic operators.
item.dc:creator: Adam Black, David Damanik, Jake Fillman, Giorgio Young

item.title: A Proof of the Ovals Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.31665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the lowest eigenvalue of the periodic Schr\"odinger operator $-\partial_s^2+\kappa^2$ on a closed curve of length $\ell$ is at least $4\pi^2/\ell^2$. Equality holds precisely for the family of ovals described by Benguria and Loss. The proof uses a new comparison argument for scalar ordinary differential equations.
item.dc:creator: Durvudkhan Suragan

item.title: A Spectral Zoo of Genus-Zero Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces with Many Boundary Components
item.description: arXiv:2611.31936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study critical points of the length-normalized first Steklov eigenvalue $\bar\sigma_1$ on genus-zero surfaces with $b$ boundary components. By a theorem of Fraser and Schoen, their first eigenfunctions give free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit ball. After uniformization, the domain is the round sphere minus $b$ round caps, with a weight on the boundary circles. A layer potential formulation gives the eigenvalues, their derivatives and a certificate for each critical point, and an exact multipole system for the caps. We compute a spectral zoo of 268 numerically certified critical points with up to $b=2252$ boundary components, including the $27$ embedded examples listed by Schulz. With their symmetry groups and Morse indices, the critical points satisfy a signed count for $3\le b\le10$. Most belong to families built from rings of boundary components. As the rings fill in, these appear to converge to the free curve minimal surfaces of Karpukhin and Noutchegueme, unions of flat disks and catenoidal annuli that meet along circles on the sphere. We construct these limits, among them the critical drum and the cake stand, a flat disk with a catenoidal horn. The families approach their limits like $j^{-1}$ for rings of $j$ caps, and the equatorial family approaches $4\pi$ with deficit $4\pi b^{-1}e^{-b}$. For large $b$, the leading terms of the multipole system reduce to the logarithmic energy of the cap centers and a formal evaluation gives $\bar\sigma_1^\star(b)=8\pi-16\pi\,b^{-1}\log b+O(b^{-1})$.
item.dc:creator: Haoyu Chen, Braxton Osting

item.title: The polygonal Steklov--Weinstock inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.32028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every integer $N \ge 3$, the regular $N$-gon uniquely maximizes the scale-invariant first positive Steklov eigenvalue $L(P)\sigma_1(P)$ among all simple planar polygons $P$ of positive area with at most $N$ sides, up to similarity (and up to congruence at prescribed perimeter). Our proof combines two complementary realizations of the Rayleigh--Ritz variational principle. For convex competitors, we transplant a first Steklov eigenfunction of the regular reference polygon: for triangles, affine transplantation aligned with a longest side yields both the sharp inequality and a two-sided linear stability bound in terms of the maximal side-length deviation; for convex $N$-gons with $N \ge 4$, a piecewise harmonic fan transplantation across radial sectors matches traces along the internal seams. In the quadrilateral case, centering the fan at the vertex average pairs opposite sides and controls the displacement of the diagonal midpoints, whereas for $N=5$ the spectral deficit dominates both the area deficit and the squared vertex and Hausdorff distances to the regular pentagon. Nonconvex competitors are treated by stratifying them according to their number $p \le N-1$ of strictly convex corners: boundary moment inequalities handle $p=3$, while conformal disk tests localized on the gaps between positive turning prevertices rule out $p \ge 4$ via comparison with the regular $(p+1)$-gon. Finite parameter ranges are certified using exact rational arithmetic and outward-rounded integer interval enclosures. In addition, we establish the sharp fourth-order asymptotic expansion of the spectral deficit at a prescribed positive-corner count, together with a quantitative local and global stability theorem for polygons with a large number of sides.
item.dc:creator: Zhuo Cheng, Yian Zhang

item.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for the First Nonzero Steklov Eigenvalue of the Witten Laplacian on Weighted Surfaces with Nonnegative Bakry-Emery-Ricci Tensor
item.description: arXiv:2611.31702v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider compact connected weighted surfaces with smooth boundary whose Bakry-Emery-Ricci tensor is nonnegative. We assume that the geodesic curvature of the boundary is bounded below in terms of the normal and tangential derivatives of the weight function. Under these assumptions, we prove a lower bound for the first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue of the Witten Laplacian, which is sharp in the sense that equality holds if and only if the surface is isometric to a Euclidean disk and the weight function is constant.
item.dc:creator: Artem M. Danilov

item.title: Verified two-sided bounds for the inf-sup constant of the divergence on planar polygons
item.description: arXiv:2611.31734v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The inf-sup constant $\beta(\Omega)$ of the divergence governs the stability of the Stokes problem. For polygons, analytic lower bounds are far from the true value, and numerical methods either bound $\beta$ from above or require spectral-gap and mesh-fineness hypotheses that cannot presently be checked. We propose a method that produces verified lower bounds without any such hypothesis. It rests on the Friedrichs formulation of $\beta$ in the Bergman space and on a multiplier identity that controls the non-compact corner contribution pointwise, with the sharp corner constant; the remaining compact part is bounded by a finite matrix inequality that is checked in exact and ball arithmetic. We prove that the bounds converge to $\beta$. Together with enclosed Rayleigh quotients of explicit trial functions (and, for the square, the bottom $\frac12-\frac1\pi$ of the essential spectrum) this yields two-sided enclosures, e.g.\ $0.426245\le\beta\le0.426252$ for the square and $0.303973\le\beta\le0.304078$ for the L-shaped domain. For a square with a square hole, which is neither simply connected nor star-shaped, we obtain $0.154596\le\beta\le0.154781$. For the rectangles $(0,1)\times(0,r)$ we enclose $\beta$ for eight aspect ratios and prove for the five ratios $r\in\{\frac14,\frac38,\frac12,\frac9{16},\frac58\}$ that $\beta^2$ is an isolated eigenvalue below the essential spectrum; the last two lie beyond the range covered by the explicit bound of Costabel, Crouzeix, Dauge and Lafranche. As an application, the certified values give guaranteed a posteriori bounds for Taylor--Hood approximations of the Stokes equations, including the doubly connected domain, for which, to our knowledge, no explicit lower bound for $\beta$ had been available.
item.dc:creator: Xuefeng Liu

item.title: Exact transport exponents for random mosaic operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.32132v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the exponentially time-averaged transport exponents of period-two random mosaic operators, with zero potential on the even sites and iid potential on the odd sites. For every bounded, strictly positive, nonconstant single-site law, on one event of probability one, $\beta_f^-(q)=\beta_f^+(q)=\max\{0,2/3-\nu_H(f)/(3q)\}$ for all nonzero finitely supported states $f$ and all $q>0$. The positive odd integer $\nu_H(f)$ is determined by divisibility by $H$ and cancellation against the bounded zero-energy solution. In particular, the large-moment exponent is $2/3$ for every such state, while point sources on the two sublattices have second-moment growth powers $1$ and $1/3$. We obtain matching resolvent bounds by retaining the vanishing orders of two polynomial source channels through the singular normalization at zero energy. We also prove deterministic lower bounds for every bounded positive configuration. No density assumption is imposed on the law.
item.dc:creator: Fumihiko Nakano, Xu Xia

item.title: A direct majorant and an improved Huber constant on cofinite Fuchsian groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.32398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: To obtain an effective upper bound for Huber's constant on cofinite Fuchsian groups, we introduce an algorithm that bypasses the quantitative Karamata Tauberian theorem in estimating spectral-counting growth by direct use of re-optimized Gaussian kernel instead. Further steps involve the different choice of a compactly supported test function, keeping linear and constant terms in the spectral estimate, optimizing the exact cusp geometry, and retaining the full explicit primitive-geodesic majorant in subsequent Chebyshev estimates. The more direct path is established to control the difference between the size of the hyperbolic term in the Selberg trace formula and the second Chebyshev function. Finally, the self-improvement device combined with a knowledge of low-lying spectral data leads to the sharpening that in the case of $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ reads $C_{\mathrm{Hub},\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z}) }<199$. The improvement factor is greater than $8.3\cdot10^{10}$ compared to what was claimed by the initial algorithm and greater than $1.1\cdot10^6$ compared to the currently known bound.
item.dc:creator: Muharem Avdispahi\'{c}

item.title: Twisted Poincar\'e series at zero on surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.32648v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(\Sigma,g)$ be a closed, connected, oriented, Riemannian Anosov surface. We show that there exists an open subset $\mathcal V_g$ of the space of finite-dimensional irreducible representations of the fundamental group of $\Sigma$, whose complement has complex codimension at least one, such that the following holds: for all $x,y\in \Sigma$, $\rho \in \mathcal{V}_g$, the meromorphic extension of the twisted Poincar\'e series $s \mapsto \eta_{g,\rho,x,y}(s)$ vanishes at $s=0$. We also give examples of non-trivial representations whose Poincar\'e series does not vanish at zero. In addition, we describe the structure of twisted resonant states at zero for these examples and show that they admit non-trivial Jordan blocks.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Humbert, Thibault Lefeuvre, Sebasti\'an Mu\~noz-Thon, Zhongkai Tao

item.title: Bloch Discriminants of Discrete Periodic Operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.33025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Bloch variety of an operator on a periodic graph encodes the relation between its spectrum and the group action on the graph, with critical points corresponding to edges of the spectrum. We adapt methods from computational algebraic geometry to describe how the qualitative behavior of critical points of Bloch varieties depends upon parameters for three Z^2-periodic graphs. The set of parameters where the qualitative behavior changes is the Bloch discriminant. As the critical points are real-algebraic with respect to a non-standard real structure on the complex torus, this is also a first step towards developing computational tools for varieties with a non-standard real structure.
item.dc:creator: Margaret H. Regan, Frank Sottile, Simon Telen

item.title: Eigenvalues of the tetradiagonal Toeplitz matrices with diagonals 1, 0, 0, 1
item.description: arXiv:2607.27684v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We perform a thorough analysis of the eigenvalues of tetradiagonal Toeplitz matrices of large order $n$ generated by the Laurent polynomial $a(t)=t^2+t^{-1}$. The spectra of these matrices are invariant under $2\pi/3$-rotation. They are contained in three segments of the complex plane and asymptotically fill these segments as $n$ tends to infinity. We apply Widom's formula for the determinants and transform the characteristic equation into a convenient form that can be solved by the fixed point iteration method. The main results are asymptotic formulas for the eigenvalues, both close to the origin and far from the origin. The main results are verified by numerical tests for moderate values of $n$.
item.dc:creator: Sergei M. Grudsky, Rom\'an Higuera-Garc\'ia, Egor A. Maximenko, Fidel V\'asquez-Rojas

item.title: Two-scale band geometry and ballistic transport for limit-periodic Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.01303v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with bounded limit-periodic potentials. If the nested periodic approximants satisfy $\|V-V_n\|_\infty=o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-\eta p_n})$, with $\eta>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, then the rescaled Heisenberg position has a nonzero strong limit on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. In contrast to earlier continuum results requiring exponential accuracy in $p_{n+1}$, the exponential weight here involves only $p_n$; the ratios $p_{n+1}/p_n$ may be unbounded. Folding identifies each ordered large-cell band, away from symmetry momenta, with a fixed translated small-cell band. This confines near-collisions of all bands to a common neighborhood controlled at the smaller period. A period-uniform quadratic-form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a graph-norm comparison linear in the potential error then give the limiting velocity. Moments of orders $0<r\le4$ have two-sided ballistic growth as a corollary. An explicit example separates the two approximation conditions.
item.dc:creator: Moises Gomez Solis

item.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.22703v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operators with a periodic background and independent Bernoulli disorder. We ask for the least background period permitting infinitely many gaps in the almost sure spectrum. We provide explicit rational parameters at the minimum period of three, answering Wood's question. Our example gives negative answers to Bellissard's question for a disconnected background hull and to Damanik and Fillman's two finite-gap questions for transitive subshifts of finite type and subshifts of positive entropy. The proof, which appears to be new, normalizes the first background value to zero and establishes a transverse heteroclinic connection at nonzero energy. A strict scale window yields invariant multicones. For every nondegenerate Bernoulli law, gaps accumulate from the right at this spectral point. This accumulation persists under small perturbations, with its energy varying real analytically. Spectral intervals approach this point from the right, ruling out a Cantor spectrum. Three is the least background period at which exact recovery of the spectrum from periodic realizations can require unbounded fundamental periods of the total potential.
item.dc:creator: Cong Chen, Yong Li

item.title: Inverse problems for ZS operators and their isomorphisms, II
item.description: arXiv:2611.28652v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators on the unit interval with generic boundary conditions. A unitary gauge transformation reduces these problems to the corresponding problems with basic boundary conditions, with an explicit shift of the spectral parameter. Using previous results for canonical boundary conditions and four-spectra data mapping we describe isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators. Moreover, we study other inverse problems including replacing mappings and canonical relations.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Korotyaev, Zongfeng Zhang

item.title: Eigenvalues of doubly stochastic matrices in large orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.30905v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $1\le k\le N$, every point in the convex hull of the $k$th roots of unity is an eigenvalue of some doubly stochastic matrix of order $N$. Perfect and Mirsky asked whether any other eigenvalues occur. We prove that the union of these polygons is the whole region for every $N\ge450$. Our pencil-and-paper proof for $N\ge10^{30}$ starts with an eigenvector $v$ of Euclidean norm one. Place one unit of mass at each coordinate $v_j$. If $Av=zv$, row $i$ draws mass $A_{ij}$ from each mark $v_j$, so the mass it receives has centre $zv_i$. The column sums ensure that each mark supplies one unit in total. It follows that the sum of the row variances is $1-|z|^2$. Since the regular $N$-gon contains the disk of radius $\cos(\pi/N)$, an eigenvalue outside the polygons would force this sum below $\sin^2(\pi/N)$. We use this bound to compare permutations of the outer marks and to follow a randomly chosen mark through a quarter turn. To reach $450$, we count marks between concentric circles and verify a finite set of inequalities by computer. We also determine the regions in orders five and six by computer-assisted proofs. At order five the full region is obtained by adding to the polygons the segments from the origin to two conjugate arcs traced by roots of quartic polynomials. At order six the square, pentagon and hexagon give the whole region.
item.dc:creator: Brecht Verbeken, Vincent Ginis

item.title: Plunge bounds for Fourier concentration operators: geometry, smoothing, and wave packets
item.description: arXiv:2610.09406v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a single-logarithm bound for the eigenvalues in the plunge region of Fourier concentration operators, removing the extra logarithmic factor in the Kulikov--Dam Larsen bound for two general admissible sets throughout each fixed exponential window. For bounded spatial and frequency sets $A,B\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of positive measure with finite upper codimension-one Minkowski boundary content, the number $\Lambda_\varepsilon(cA,B)$ of eigenvalues in $(\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)$ satisfies $\Lambda_\varepsilon(cA,B)\le C(d,A,B,\beta)c^{d-1}D(1+\log_+(c/D))$, where $D=\log(1/(\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)))$, for every fixed $\beta>0$, $c\ge2$, $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and $D\le\beta c$, with $\log_+t=\max(0,\log t)$. The argument uses positive band-limited smoothing and requires no symmetry, convexity, or connectedness. In dimension two, the corresponding exponential-window estimate has a constant uniform in the window parameter. We also determine the optimal coordinate-Lipschitz constant $d-1$ for recursive decompositions of balls and standard simplices in every dimension, and obtain box-frequency estimates with explicit geometric constants. For $C^1$ convex bodies in three dimensions, the optimal infimum of recursive coordinate slopes is $2$. Uniform real-order Bessel estimates give independent disk and ball bounds at every spectral threshold, including an explicit deep-tail term. For smooth strictly convex planar frequency bodies with positive curvature, we prove correlation estimates for aligned Gaussian packets at arbitrary relative scales and quantitative lower bounds on the cost of estimating spatial blocks separately. Together these results connect the global spectral bound with sharp geometric constructions and the cancellation retained by grouping boundary interactions.
item.dc:creator: Ahmadreza Azimifard

item.title: Strict hot spots and absence of interior critical points on simply connected planar H\"older domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.29324v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Every nonzero real eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue on a bounded simply connected planar H\"older domain has no interior critical point. The H\"older condition is quasihyperbolic; equivalently, a Riemann map has derivative in $L^{2p}$ for some $p>1$. This includes Lipschitz domains and polygons with reentrant corners. Multiple eigenvalues and non-Jordan boundaries are allowed. The proof uses boundary primitives, a uniform multiplier estimate, and approximation of the whole limiting eigenspace. When this eigenspace is two-dimensional, every real basis gives global coordinates onto a domain star-shaped about the origin. A stream function proves injectivity and yields a Poisson formula for the boundary angular derivative. The conformal boundary map has a Lipschitz inverse and a rectifiable Jordan image; its boundary angle is a circle diffeomorphism with nonvanishing H\"older-continuous derivative. The image can be nonconvex even when the source is smooth and strictly convex.
item.dc:creator: Yutian Li
